title: A torus-normalized operator algebra has a torus-stable simple submodule
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $T$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Let $M\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and let $\tau:T\to\operatorname{GL}(M)$ be a rational representation, meaning a group-scheme homomorphism with $\operatorname{GL}(M)(R)=\operatorname{Aut}_R(M\otimes_kR)$. Let $B\subseteq\operatorname{End}_k(M)$ be a unital $k$-subalgebra. Suppose for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $t\in T(R)$ that $\tau_R(t)(B\otimes_kR)\tau_R(t)^{-1}=B\otimes_kR$. Then there is a nonzero $k$-linear subspace $U\subseteq M$ such that $BU\subseteq U$, the only $B$-stable $k$-linear subspaces of $U$ are $0,U$, and $\tau_R(t)(U\otimes_kR)=U\otimes_kR$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $t\in T(R)$. No semisimplicity assumption on the $B$-module $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent auxiliary lemma from the Grassmannian and projectivity in Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Borel fixed point Corollary 17.3, printed p.353: apply the latter to the closed locus of submodules of the least positive possible dimension. The precise operator-algebra statement is not a verbatim theorem in Milne.

proof.text: Put $n=\dim_k M>0$. The set of dimensions of nonzero $B$-stable subspaces of $M$ is a nonempty subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, since $M$ itself belongs to it. Let $d$ be its least element and choose a $B$-stable subspace $W$ of dimension $d$. Every $B$-stable subspace of $M$ of dimension $d$ is simple: any nonzero proper subspace stable under $B$ would have dimension strictly between $0$ and $d$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary argument from Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Corollary 17.3, printed p.353.

proof.text: Choose a basis $M\simeq k^n$. Apply [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective] with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and quotient rank $n-d$. Its projective scheme $G$ parametrizes rank-$(n-d)$ locally free quotients of $M\otimes_k\mathcal O_Y$ on every $k$-scheme $Y$. Write $q:M\otimes_k\mathcal O_G\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal Q$ for its universal quotient, and $\mathcal S=\ker q$. Locally trivialize $\mathcal Q$ and restrict to the locus where a chosen $(n-d)$-minor of the surjection matrix is invertible. After changing its target frame that matrix is $[I\ A]$; its kernel consists of $(-Av,v)$, with $v$ in a free module of rank $d$. Thus $\mathcal S$ is locally free of rank $d$, the surjection is locally split, and its split exact sequence remains exact under every base change. Conversely a rank-$d$ locally direct summand gives such a quotient. Thus $G$ also parametrizes those subbundles, including $d=n$, where $G=\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary argument from Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Corollary 17.3, printed p.353.

proof.text: The algebra $B$ is finite-dimensional, since it is a linear subspace of $\operatorname{End}_k(M)$. Choose a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $B$ and form the bundle map $D:\mathcal S\to\mathcal Q^{\oplus s}$ with components $q\circ b_j|_{\mathcal S}$. On an affine open where both bundles are free, [lem-sc-affine-free-map-zero-locus] represents the condition $h^*D=0$ by the closed subscheme cut out by the finitely many matrix entries. Vanishing of a sheaf morphism is local on the source, so [lem-sc-local-closed-locus-gluing] glues these loci to a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow G$, locally of finite presentation. Its functor on every $k$-scheme $Y$ is precisely the rank-$d$ locally direct summands $L\subseteq M\otimes_k\mathcal O_Y$ with $b_jL\subseteq L$ for all $j$. These conditions are equivalent to $B\otimes_k\mathcal O_Y$ preserving $L$, since the $b_j$ span $B$. This is a scheme-theoretic zero locus, not just a closed set of rational points.

source.place: Agent auxiliary argument from Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Corollary 17.3, printed p.353.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $G$ is proper over $k$. A closed immersion is proper and composites of proper morphisms are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], hence $X$ is proper over $k$. In particular it is of finite type, by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The subspace $W$ selected in step 1 gives a $k$-point of $X$, so $X$ is nonempty. We make no assertion that $X$ is reduced, smooth, or connected.

source.place: Agent auxiliary argument from Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Corollary 17.3, printed p.353.

proof.text: The representation defines an action on $G$: on a commutative $k$-algebra $R$, send a locally direct summand $L\subseteq M\otimes_kR$ to $gL$, where $g=\tau_R(t)$. Its quotient is identified with the original quotient by $g^{-1}$, so its rank is unchanged. These assignments commute with scalar extension, and the representing property in [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective] gives the action morphism (equivalently apply the construction to the universal automorphism and subbundle on $T\times_kG$). If $L$ is $B_R$-stable, then for $b\in B_R$, $\ell\in L$ one has $b(g\ell)=g((g^{-1}bg)\ell)\in gL$, since the normalization hypothesis gives $g^{-1}bg\in B_R$. This holds over every $R$, and locally over every $k$-scheme; the universal map on $T\times_kX$ therefore has zero pulled-back $D$. The factorization criterion of [lem-sc-local-closed-locus-gluing] factors it through $X$. The identity and multiplication identities follow from those of $\tau$ and uniqueness of this factorization. We have constructed an action of $T$ on the scheme $X$, with its full possible nonreduced structure.

source.place: Agent auxiliary argument from Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Corollary 17.3, printed p.353.

proof.text: The split torus $T$ is smooth and connected by the clause "Every torus is smooth and connected" in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. It is affine and of finite type: the coordinate description of $\mathbf G_m$ in [def-sc-gm-ga] gives $T\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k[x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r]/(x_iy_i-1:1\leq i\leq r)$. It is commutative, so its first commutator subgroup is trivial and it is solvable. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] now hold for its action on the nonempty proper finite-type scheme $X$. Obtain $x\in X(k)$ fixed scheme-theoretically: $t\cdot x_R=x_R$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $t\in T(R)$. This also covers $r=0$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary argument from Propositions 7.29--7.30, printed p.146, and Corollary 17.3, printed p.353.

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq M$ be the subspace classified by $x$. By step 3 it is $B$-stable and has dimension $d>0$. It is simple by the minimality argument in step 1. Since equality of points of $X(R)$ means equality of the corresponding subbundles of $M\otimes_kR$, the fixed-point identity in step 6 is exactly $\tau_R(t)(U\otimes_kR)=U\otimes_kR$. This proves every clause, without using semisimplicity of $M$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NQ-88e784e58 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes, no new nodes; full review in review.md. The statement is unchanged and true: a Lie–Kolchin-style argument (Milne 17.4) applying Borel's fixed-point theorem to minimal B-stable subspaces. I checked Milne iAG2017 7.29–7.30 (printed p.146) and 17.1–17.3 (printed p.353) in the PDF. It matches how the parent lem-sfb-normalized-algebra-weight-line-simple uses it in its step 4. Live and side-live still show the item unsplit and unreviewed, there is no repair note, and the DAG has no duplicate. Steps: (1) the least positive dimension d of a B-stable subspace exists and every d-dimensional one is simple, which is elementary. (2) The Grassmann node gives the quotient Grassmannian of rank n−d; the [I A] minor chart shows the kernel S is locally free of rank d and split, so it commutes with base change. (3) The zero locus of D=(q∘b_j|S)_j is built with the affine free-map zero-locus node on free affine opens and glued with the gluing node, whose locality hypotheses hold; it is scheme-theoretic. (4) Projective implies proper, plus closed immersion and composition, gives X proper and of finite type; W gives a k-point. (5) The T-action is q↦q∘τ(t)^{-1}, and b(gℓ)=g((g^{-1}bg)ℓ) holds over every R, so it factors through X by the gluing node's universal property. (6) Every hypothesis of the solvable fixed-point node holds: T is a torus, hence smooth and connected; it is affine of finite type by def-sc-gm-ga; it is commutative, hence solvable; X is nonempty, proper and of finite type. (7) The fixed point x gives a simple U with τ_R(t)(U⊗R)=U⊗R. Small cases checked: n=1; B=k (X=P(M)); d=n; r=0; the nonreduced k[N] example, whose locus a^2=0 is preserved by a↦a/t. Accepted tool uses: affine-free-map-zero-locus, local-closed-locus-gluing, pc-projective-proper and the proper-permanence Mathlib leaf, all generic.
